season_storylines: The QB carousel resets the position: Tua Tagovailoa took a league-minimum deal in Atlanta ahead of Michael Penix Jr.'s ACL rehab, Kyler Murray was named Minnesota's starter over J.J. McCarthy, Kirk Cousins is backing up No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza in Las Vegas, and Malik Willis holds Miami's job, so late-round 6-pt-TD QB targets are unusually murky and rushing QBs are the safe ceiling play.

A.J. Brown is now a Patriot after New England's Super Bowl run, giving Drake Maye a true alpha deep threat and boosting his 6-pt-TD stock, while Philadelphia's pass game loses TD equity and Jalen Hurts' career-high passing TD rate is a regression candidate under new OC Sean Mannion.

Seven new head coaches shuffle scheme value: John Harbaugh to the Giants, Mike McCarthy to Pittsburgh, Kevin Stefanski to Atlanta, Todd Monken to Cleveland, Robert Saleh to Tennessee, Klint Kubiak to Las Vegas, Jeff Hafley to Miami, plus Mike McDaniel landing as Chargers OC where his run-game design points Omarion Hampton at RB1 volume.

Daniel Jones' Achilles tear guts the Colts' passing game; Jonathan Taylor faces loaded boxes and a downgraded scoring environment, and Keenan Allen's signing plus Alec Pierce's pending PUP return are patches, not fixes.

The mid-August injury wave is repricing drafts: Ricky Pearsall (PCL) is out for the season in San Francisco, Kyle Monangai's hyperextended knee puts his Week 1 in doubt in Chicago, Breece Hall's groin (2-3 weeks) and Chuba Hubbard's hamstring are week-to-week, Emeka Egbuka's toe threatens Week 1, and Luther Burden III will miss the preseason.

The 35-yard-line touchback rule has kept kickoff returns at roughly double the old rate, so locked-in returners like Rashid Shaheed (SEA), Zachariah Branch (ATL), and Malik Washington (verify team) carry a real 2.5-3.4 ppg edge in return-yardage leagues like this one.

Betting markets flag New England (10.5, models near 11.8) and Jacksonville (9.5 after a 13-4 season) as the big overs, while Baltimore 11.5, Tennessee 7.5, and Green Bay 10.5 are the sharpest fades, useful team-total context for stacking and DST picks.

Malik Nabers is back at practice after ACL rehab and tracks toward Week 1 with a worst case of missing a game or two, making his depressed ADP one of the few blue-chip discounts on the board despite a rookie QB in Jaxson Dart.

Cleveland's Deshaun Watson vs. Shedeur Sanders battle is genuinely open, with each starting a preseason game and Todd Monken's historically pass-heavy, TE-friendly scheme raising the stakes for Harold Fannin and the whole Browns pass game.
Aaron Donald is working out at the Rams facility weighing a comeback and Vita Vea is holding out in Tampa with a trade request, two defensive-line dominoes that move DST big-play value on both sides.

teams.outlook: New HC Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett install a McVay-style, multi-TE offense but a three-way QB mess (Brissett contract standoff, Minshew, rookie Carson Beck) and a 4.5 win total cap everyone, including Marvin Harrison Jr.'s TD equity.

Kevin Stefanski and OC Tommy Rees bring a TE-friendly, run-anchored scheme with Tua likely opening at QB and Penix looming mid-season, so Bijan's volume is safe while returner Zachariah Branch adds sneaky return-yardage juice.

New HC Jesse Minter and Payton-tree OC Declan Doyle keep Lamar Jackson's rushing floor elite for 6-pt-TD scoring, but models fade the 11.5 win total by over two wins after an 8-9 season, so team TDs may be scarcer than priced.

Joe Brady takes over as HC with Pete Carmichael at OC in a balanced attack that keeps James Cook's TD-heavy role gold in non-PPR, while Josh Allen's six-year-low passing marks and late-2025 foot injury make him a price-not-player question.

Rico Dowdle won the starting RB job outright and Chuba Hubbard's hamstring is week-to-week, so the goal-line and early-down work that non-PPR rewards runs through Dowdle with Jonathon Brooks the rising contingency.

Ben Johnson's offense is projected among the league's fewest pass attempts, concentrating value in the run game where Kyle Monangai's knee (Week 1 in doubt) hands D'Andre Swift the early workload, and Luther Burden's groin boosts Rome Odunze.
The pass-first core stays intact but the market's 10.5 win total (models nearer 9) implies shootout-prone games, which keeps Bengals passing-game TD equity high even if team success lags (verify).
Todd Monken's pass-heavy scheme arrives with an open Watson-vs-Shedeur Sanders QB battle, a TE-precedent boost for Harold Fannin, and a Judkins-Sampson committee clouded by Judkins' fibula history.

Mike McCarthy's exit leaves a reset staff with an unsettled left tackle battle and a 9.5 win total models see as too high, so treat Cowboys skill players as volume plays in a lower-scoring environment than recent vintage (verify).

A steady 10.5 win total with model agreement marks Denver as a trustworthy scoring environment, though Courtland Sutton shows up on fade lists and Travis Hunter's listed move to Denver needs confirmation (verify).

New OC Drew Petzing is a run-game specialist, which supports the backfield but tightens the pass pie: Jared Goff loses schemed efficiency, Jameson Williams' 17% target share plus a shoulder issue and Sam LaPorta's return make Lions WRs TD-dependent.

Models fade Green Bay by over two wins after talent departures, and Josh Jacobs is a classic post-300-touch decline candidate behind a bottom-tier line with MarShawn Lloyd lurking, while Tucker Kraft's ACL return may be snap-managed early.
A clean 10.5 win total with model agreement keeps the passing offense investable, though Tank Dell's latest knee issue again pushes his deep-threat role toward late-round lottery status.

Daniel Jones' Achilles injury flips the Colts run-heavy by necessity, so Jonathan Taylor keeps volume but loses scoring environment, and Keenan Allen plus a returning Alec Pierce are efficiency bandaids on a compromised pass game.

Coming off 13-4 with markets still pricing only 9.5 wins, Jacksonville is a buy-the-environment team, though the backfield (LeQuint Allen soft-tissue, goal-line pecking order) and Travis Hunter's role need preseason clarity (verify).

Patrick Mahomes is managing a knee issue but targets Week 1, and with a +34 point differential last year the bounce-back is real yet fully priced at 10.5, while Kelce's slipping ADP reflects an aging target tree.

Mike McDaniel as OC is the quiet scheme win of the offseason: his motion-heavy run designs have repeatedly produced lethal ground games, positioning Omarion Hampton for RB1 volume and the goal-line work this format pays for.

The league's highest win total (12.5) meets regression math: Stafford's career-high 7.7% TD rate should cool, Davante Adams (33) was TD-dependent, Puka's groin is called minor, and Blake Corum is eating into Kyren Williams' goal-line role.

Klint Kubiak's Shanahan-tree offense with No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza expected under center by Week 1-3 sets up Brock Bowers as the featured weapon and gives Ashton Jeanty both early-down and pass-game volume.

A 4.5 win total with Malik Willis at QB screams negative scripts, and Willis' historically tiny RB target rate dents De'Von Achane's receiving path, though Achane's rush yardage and Keaton Mitchell's explosiveness still play in non-PPR.
Kyler Murray was named the starter over J.J. McCarthy, adding a rushing floor to a Kevin O'Connell passing tree that keeps Justin Jefferson's yardage ceiling intact in a 9.5-win-range offense.

The market's biggest over (10.5 line, models near 11.8) after a Super Bowl appearance, and A.J. Brown's arrival gives Drake Maye a deep-ball TD amplifier, while Rhamondre Stevenson's late-2025 snap edge tempers TreVeyon Henderson hype.

An 8.5 win total models slash toward 6.8 signals a thin scoring environment, and rookie WR Jordyn Tyson's two-month hamstring timeline with possible IR removes the buzziest upside piece from early drafts (verify).

John Harbaugh brings adult supervision with Matt Nagy calling plays for Jaxson Dart, whose rushing gives 6-pt-TD appeal despite INT risk, and Malik Nabers' ACL rehab tracking toward Week 1 makes him the roster's discounted centerpiece.

Frank Reich's OC arrival can't hide a 5.5 win total, but Breece Hall (groin, back for the opener) and Garrett Wilson still command the kind of volume that survives bad offense, with Braelon Allen the handcuff to know.

Losing A.J. Brown and installing first-time OC Sean Mannion puts Hurts' career-high passing TD rate on regression watch, concentrating the offense back through Saquon Barkley and Hurts' goal-line rushing, tush-push permitting.

Mike McCarthy's proven system is expected to consolidate the backfield around Jaylen Warren in a near-workhorse role, while the DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. pairing works through August dings (verify Pittman fit).

Pearsall's season-ending PCL surgery forced a veteran patch of Deebo Samuel and Mike Evans around CMC's age-30, post-400-touch profile, with Kittle fighting to clear PUP for the Week 1 Australia opener and Christian Kirk nursing a calf.

An 11.5 win total with model agreement makes Seattle a premium environment even as Kubiak departs, and Rashid Shaheed's deep-threat-plus-kick-returner combo is exactly what this league's return-yardage and yardage-over-catches scoring pays.

New OC Zac Robinson inherits Egbuka's uncertain toe (Godwin and McMillan benefit if he sits), a Bucky Irving efficiency question with Sean Tucker goal-line work and Kenneth Gainwell added, and a Vita Vea holdout distracting the defense.

Robert Saleh with OC Brian Daboll is a defense-first reset, models slash the 7.5 win total to near 5, and Cam Ward's shoulder plus a bottom-three line make every Titan a volume-risk fade, especially a committee-bound Tony Pollard.

Continuity OC David Blough keeps Jayden Daniels' rushing-driven ceiling alive despite passing regression whispers, and Stefon Diggs' August 5 signing slots him as the clear No. 2 behind Terry McLaurin.

breakout_watch.name: Omarion Hampton
breakout_watch.why: Mike McDaniel's Chargers run scheme has a track record of manufacturing elite ground games, and Hampton's projected early-down plus goal-line volume is exactly what non-PPR pays premium for.

breakout_watch.name: Jaylen Warren
breakout_watch.why: Mike McCarthy's arrival in Pittsburgh points to a consolidated near-workhorse role, and touch volume plus goal-line access beats any catch-count concern in this format.

breakout_watch.name: Ashton Jeanty
breakout_watch.why: Klint Kubiak's Shanahan-tree offense in Las Vegas plans to add pass-game usage to his feature-back workload, and the total-yardage load carries TD equity even on a rebuilding team.

breakout_watch.name: Brock Bowers
breakout_watch.why: Kubiak's scheme is set to feature him as the offense's centerpiece, and a No. 1 target role with red-zone gravity gives TE-position leverage.

breakout_watch.name: Rashid Shaheed
breakout_watch.why: Locked-in Seattle kick returner with a legit deep-threat role: return yardage at 1/20 plus 6-pt return TDs plus air-yardage spikes make him worth 2-3 ppg more here than standard leagues.

breakout_watch.name: Zachariah Branch
breakout_watch.why: Atlanta's primary KR/PR with college return TDs on both units; in this scoring a full-time return role alone is startable-adjacent flex value with return-TD lottery tickets.

breakout_watch.name: Rome Odunze
breakout_watch.why: Luther Burden's groin injury clears preseason reps and early-season targets, and Odunze's downfield profile beats slot-compiler value in a zero-PPR league.

breakout_watch.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
breakout_watch.why: Ricky Pearsall's season-ending PCL surgery opened a real 49ers rotation path, and camp buzz has him climbing boards as a free-square late pick.

breakout_watch.name: Jonathon Brooks
breakout_watch.why: Chuba Hubbard's week-to-week hamstring plus Brooks' returning health give him a path to early-season touches behind Rico Dowdle in Carolina.

breakout_watch.name: Dylan Sampson
breakout_watch.why: Led all RBs in yards per route last year on a small sample, and Quinshon Judkins' fibula-fracture history plus Monken's pass-heavy scheme give Sampson standalone yardage value.

breakout_watch.name: Harold Fannin
breakout_watch.why: Todd Monken's offenses have a strong receiving-TE precedent, and his recent ADP dip makes the entry price better than the role.

breakout_watch.name: Jaxson Dart
breakout_watch.why: Rushing-heavy profile under Harbaugh/Nagy fits 6-pt passing TDs plus rushing yardage, though the -2 INT penalty means treat him as an upside QB2, not a locked starter.

breakout_watch.name: Blake Corum
breakout_watch.why: Out-producing Kyren Williams on efficiency and taking goal-line work in the league's highest-total offense; goal-line RB shares in non-PPR are the cheapest TDs on the board.

fade_watch.name: Christian McCaffrey
fade_watch.why: Age-30 season coming off 400+ touches, a historical near-zero repeat-top-5 profile, declining rush efficiency, and he lost Kittle's blocking for part of camp; the price still assumes prime CMC.

fade_watch.name: Davante Adams
fade_watch.why: 33 years old with a career-low catch rate and career-low YAC, and 15 TDs on an unsustainable spike; in a TD-and-yardage league you are paying for last year's regression fuel.

fade_watch.name: Josh Jacobs
fade_watch.why: Post-300-touch decline pattern, knee and calf injuries last season, a bottom-six offensive line, models slashing Green Bay's wins, and MarShawn Lloyd behind him.

fade_watch.name: Jared Goff
fade_watch.why: Zero rushing production in a league scoring passing at 25 yds/pt, a new run-first OC, and a 38% bust-week rate last year; pocket compilers are structurally punished here.

fade_watch.name: Jonathan Taylor
fade_watch.why: Daniel Jones' Achilles injury means stacked boxes and fewer scoring drives; the yardage floor survives non-PPR but the TD ceiling is what his ADP is charging for.

fade_watch.name: Tony Pollard
fade_watch.why: Three straight ~300-touch seasons with no top-20 finish in two years, a bottom-three line, a likely committee with Tyjae Spears and rookie Nick Singleton, and Tennessee's win total is a model fade.

fade_watch.name: Luther Burden III
fade_watch.why: Groin injury wipes his preseason, he has never topped 68% routes, and his slot-compiler profile is the exact archetype zero-PPR devalues while Colston Loveland eats red-zone targets.

fade_watch.name: Bucky Irving
fade_watch.why: Rising ADP into a bad setup: fourth-lowest rushing success rate, only 10 games last year, Sean Tucker on goal-line work, Kenneth Gainwell added, and a new OC with no loyalty to him.

fade_watch.name: De'Von Achane
fade_watch.why: Malik Willis' historically low RB target rate hits Achane's receiving yardage in a 4.5-win offense; the speed plays anywhere but the price reflects a passing-game role that may not exist (verify Willis as confirmed starter).

uncertainty_note: Genuinely unsettled as of Aug 19: the Cleveland (Watson vs Sanders) and Atlanta (Tua vs Penix timing) QB decisions, whether Mendoza starts Week 1 in Las Vegas, Week 1 availability for Egbuka, Monangai, Hubbard, Kittle, Kraft, and Nabers, Travis Hunter's team/role listing (Denver appears in ADP data but is unconfirmed), Bhayshul Tuten's team (conflicting JAX/ATL references), the Brissett contract standoff in Arizona, and the Vita Vea holdout; several sourced 2026 roster placements (Pittman in PIT, Likely in NYG, Tyson in NO) come from single outlets and are flagged (verify) where used.
